full_sentence: Every morning, my brother wakes up at six o'clock.

options.why_wrong: The verb needs an -s in the third person singular (he, she, it), so after 'my brother' we must say 'wakes'.

options.text: is waking up at six o'clock.
options.why_wrong: The present continuous describes an action happening now, but a daily routine uses the present simple.

options.text: will wake up at six o'clock tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: The future tense refers to one specific future time, but 'every morning' describes a repeated routine.

grammar_focus: Present Simple: third person singular with 'every morning' routines
explanation: The stem describes a daily routine, so the sentence needs the present simple. The subject 'my brother' is third person singular, so the verb takes an -s ending.
translation: Todas as manhãs, meu irmão acorda às seis horas.
